meta.title: OpenAEC Installer — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: OpenAEC Installer: the central hub to install, update and launch every open source OpenAEC tool. For Windows, macOS and Linux.

header.label: Every tool in one place
header.title: OpenAEC Installer
header.desc: The central hub for OpenAEC’s open source construction software. One app that knows every tool, sees what is already on your computer and installs or updates the newest official version with one click. For Windows, macOS and Linux.

cta.related: See all tools on the homepage

slides.overview: Overview of the desktop apps: for each tool a preview, the status (installed, update available or not installed), the version and buttons to launch, update or install
slides.status: Grouped by status: the installed tools at the top, two of them with an update and the old and new version side by side
slides.theme: Settings, Appearance section, with the list of colour themes

notice.text: Always the official version: the Installer fetches every tool straight from its own GitHub release, and checks the signature when the tool provides one.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Every OpenAEC tool, one app
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

catalog.title: Every tool on one screen
catalog.desc: OpenAEC’s desktop apps and web tools, each with a preview, a short description and its status on your computer. Filter by installed, by updates or by discipline (Architecture, Engineering, Construction, Infra), or search by name.

updates.title: See what needs updating, and update it all at once
updates.desc: The Installer compares the version on your computer with the newest release and shows both side by side. Update all fetches every update at once. On Windows this happens silently, in the same kind of setup as the existing installation, so a tool never ends up installed twice.

safe.title: No lost work, no stray files
safe.desc: The update is downloaded and checked while the tool stays open. Then the Installer asks you to close the tool; it never closes it itself. After the update it starts the tool again. If a tool provides a signed update file, nothing starts when the signature does not match.

look.title: In the style of open-aec.com
look.desc: The dark panel and tiles of this website, with a featured tool at the top. Choose from five themes (light, dark, Blueprint and high contrast dark or light) and three text sizes, in Dutch or English.

catalog.title: Catalogue
catalog.desc: Every OpenAEC tool with description and category: desktop apps and web tools.

filters.title: Filters and search
filters.desc: By status, by discipline or by name, so you quickly find what you are looking for.

launch.title: Launch
launch.desc: Start an installed tool straight from the Installer.

webtabs.title: Web tools in tabs
webtabs.desc: Web tools and the web versions of desktop apps open in a tab inside the Installer or in your own browser. Open tabs are remembered.

detect.title: Installation detection
detect.desc: Sees which tools are already installed and in which version: on Windows through the registry, on Linux through the managed AppImage folder.

install.title: One-click install
install.desc: The official installer from GitHub Releases, matching your operating system and processor.

silent.title: Silent updates
silent.desc: On Windows in the same kind of setup, after the tool has been closed and with a restart afterwards.

signed.title: Signature checked
signed.desc: Tools with a signed update file are only installed when the signature matches.

copies.title: Duplicate and renamed tools
copies.desc: If a tool is installed twice, both copies are updated; a tool with a new name is also recognised under that name.

self.title: Updates itself
self.desc: The Installer also checks its own version and updates itself silently.

themes.title: Five themes
themes.desc: Light, dark, Blueprint and high contrast dark or light.

lang.title: Dutch and English
lang.desc: The interface is bilingual and can be switched in Settings.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v0.2.14
download.lead: Free and without an account. Every button starts the download right away.
download.metaWindows: Installer for Windows, 64-bit, no administrator rights needed
download.metaMac: Disk image for Macs with an Apple or Intel processor
download.metaLinux: AppImage for Linux x86-64, runs on most distributions
download.mobileNote: The OpenAEC Installer is a desktop application for Windows, macOS and Linux. Download it on your computer; all files are listed below.

note.platforms: Per platform: installing, updating and launching work on Windows, through the official installers, and on Linux, through AppImages without administrator rights and with a shortcut in the menu. On macOS the catalogue and the web tools work; installing desktop apps will follow.
note.linux: Linux: make the AppImage executable once with chmod +x and then start it.

whatsnew.label: New in v0.2.14
whatsnew.title: Renamed tools keep up
whatsnew.desc: Released on 3 November 2026. This version recognises a tool that got a new name and updates it under that name, such as Open CalcSheet Studio from its new repository. The versions before it, from late October and early November, brought the new design, silent updates and signature checks.

renamed.title: New name, same tool
renamed.desc: An installed tool with an old name is recognised and updated to the version under its new name.

design.title: New design
design.desc: The dark panel and tiles of open-aec.com, with filters by status and discipline, a featured tool and Update all.

silent.title: Silent updates
silent.desc: Updates in the same kind of setup, only once the tool is closed and with a restart afterwards. The Installer itself also updates silently.

signed.title: Signatures
signed.desc: Tools with a signed update file are only installed once the signature matches.

arm.title: The right installer
arm.desc: On a PC with an x64 processor the Installer never picks an ARM installer any more.

feed.title: One release file
feed.desc: The newest versions come from a single file instead of a request per tool, so GitHub’s rate limit no longer gets in the way.

cost.a: Nothing. The OpenAEC Installer and the tools it installs are free and open source. No account is needed.

what.q: What exactly does the Installer do?
what.a: It shows every OpenAEC tool, sees which ones are already on your computer and in which version, and puts the newest official installer from GitHub Releases in place with one click. After that you also launch the tools from the Installer, and you open web tools in a tab.

platforms.q: Does it work on macOS and Linux?
platforms.a: Installing, updating and launching work on Windows, through the official installers, and on Linux, through AppImages without administrator rights and with a shortcut in the menu. On macOS the catalogue and the web tools work; installing desktop apps will follow.

work.q: Will I lose work during an update?
work.a: No. The Installer downloads and checks the update while the tool stays open, and then asks you to close it. It never closes the tool itself. If the tool was open, it starts it again after the update.

trust.q: How do I know a download is genuine?
trust.a: The Installer only fetches the official files from each tool’s GitHub release. If a tool publishes a signed update file, the Installer checks the signature while downloading and starts nothing when it is missing or does not match.

admin.a: Not for the Installer itself: it installs just for you. A tool that was installed for all users of the computer still asks for administrator rights when it is updated. On Linux it installs tools as AppImages, without administrator rights.

license.q: Which licence does the Installer use?
license.a: The Installer’s source code is licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. Every tool it installs has its own licence; you will find it on the product page and in the repository of that tool.

tech.heading: Technology and licence
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

tauri.title: Tauri 2 and Rust
tauri.desc: A Rust core handles downloads, installations, version checks and signatures.

ui.title: React and TypeScript
ui.desc: The interface follows design 0.4 of OpenAEC-Blueprint, with the tokens, fonts and icons of the house style.

releases.title: GitHub Releases
releases.desc: The versions come from a single release file; when it is missing, the Installer asks GitHub itself.

plugin.title: For app makers
plugin.desc: A Tauri plugin and a release kit let an OpenAEC app hand its updates to the Installer, with signed update files.

license.title: CC BY-SA 4.0
license.desc: The source code is on GitHub, with the issues for a problem or a request.

final.desc: One download, and every OpenAEC tool is within reach.
